subject: Peninsula Health renewal — term reset + SLA addendum request
messages:
From: Sophie Reynolds <sophie@peninsulahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@peninsulahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — concerned about costs and uptime guarantees

Logan / Rajiv,

We need to talk about our upcoming renewal. After the last quarter we’ve had a few outages and the engineering team is worried about predictable latency for certain workflows. Budget is also tighter than expected — procurement is pushing for a lower run-rate.

Right now renewal numbers put us outside the range the board will approve. We are interested in staying with Redwood but will need: a one-time credit applied to the renewal, a softened term (we were sold 24 months last renewal but would prefer a reset to 12 months with more flexible termination), and an SLA addendum that gives us material uptime credits tied to response times.

Can you share what options are on the table? We need a concrete proposal by EOD Friday so I can present to procurement.

Thanks,
Sophie Reynolds
Director of Infrastructure
Peninsula Health

Attachments: Peninsula_Renewal_Request_2028-04.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Reynolds <sophie@peninsulahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — concerned about costs and uptime guarantees

Sophie — thanks for the clarity and sorry to hear about the outages. I’ve looped in Marissa (renewals lead) and Grace (CS lead) so we can align on options quickly.

High level — we can consider: 1) a one-time credit, 2) a term reset to 12 months with a committed minimum spend to replace length, and 3) a formal SLA addendum (we’ll need to scope the credit schedule). I’ve asked Grace to collect incident post-mortem notes so we can quantify the reliability work and include that in the concession.

Can you confirm procurement’s target credit amount and whether they require the SLA to be backed with a monetary credit formula (e.g., % refund for X minutes of downtime)? I’ll aim to have an internal recommendation by Thursday EOD.

Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0123

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Peninsula Health — customer context and proposed concession package

Team — quick summary and ask.

Customer: Peninsula Health (mid-size regional health system)
Renewal date: 2028-05-15
Current ARR: $480,000 annualized (monthly billing cadence)
Churn risk: high (procurement is evaluating 2 vendors)
Primary concerns: previous outages in Feb/Mar, unpredictability of P99 latency for critical clinical workflows, and board-level budget pressure.

What the customer is asking for:
- One-time credit: $60k toward renewal
- Term reset: move from proposed 24 months back to 12 months (with a modest committed spend floor)
- SLA addendum: 99.9% uptime with monetary credits at defined thresholds; customer needs this in writing for procurement

Why we should consider concessions:
- Retention value: expected 3-year customer LTV > $1.3M — losing them would be a material gap in our regional healthcare vertical momentum
- Cost to replace: estimated ramp + migration cost for customer ~ $250k (integration + compliance work)
- PR / reference value: Peninsula is a top reference in the region; keeping them helps sales in similar accounts

Recommended Deal Desk escalation ask (what I need from you):
1) Exec approval for up to $50k one-time credit (we may ask for $60k but recommend pre-approval up to $50k)
2) Approval to permit a 12-month term reset with a minimum committed spend of $420k for the year
3) Approval to provide an SLA addendum modeled on our standard healthcare SLA with a 99.9% target and a capped credit schedule (I attach a draft for review)

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_draft.docx (docx stub), Peninsula_Renewal_Term_Sheet.pdf (pdf stub)

Please advise if I should include additional commercial levers (e.g., usage-based discount tiers) when I present to Sophie on Thursday.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: ESCALATION: Peninsula Health renewal — request for executive approval (credits / SLA / term reset)

Vivek — escalating a renewal that needs executive signoff. Context and recommended approvals below.

Summary of ask: customer is at risk of churn. Grace recommends concessions; I recommend we approve limited concessions to retain the account while protecting net revenue.

Recommended approvals:
A) One-time credit: approve up to $50,000 (customer asked $60k) — applied against renewal invoice; contingent on signing a 12-month commitment for $420k minimum spend.
B) Term reset: allow 12-month reset only (no automatic extension to 24) — require minimum spend as above and auto-convert to standard renewal terms after 12 months.
C) SLA addendum: approve execution of SLA_Addendum_draft with a capped credit schedule (max exposure to Redwood of $25k per year) — legal to redline and attachments to be finalized by Contracts.

Supporting rationale: retention at current pricing protects our healthcare go-to-market foothold; migration cost for customer is non-trivial; limited concession packaging balances commercial defense with downside exposure.

Decision needed by: Fri, 2028-04-13 COB (customer needs a formal offer).

Please reply with Approve / Decline / Approve with changes and any required modifications to the limits above.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Renewals Lead, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments included inline: Peninsula_Renewal_Term_Sheet.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Reynolds <sophie@peninsulahealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@peninsulahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ESCALATION: Peninsula Health renewal — request for executive approval (credits / SLA / term reset)

Approve with modification.

Decision (approved):
- One-time credit: APPROVED $40,000 (we will not approve full $50k requested) — to be applied to the first renewal invoice provided the customer signs the 12-month commitment by 2028-04-20.
- Term reset: APPROVED to 12 months with required minimum committed spend of $420k.
- SLA addendum: APPROVED in principle. Legal/Contracts to finalize the redline but cap our maximum exposure to $20k per year on SLA credits.

Next steps (action items):
1) Logan — present this package to Sophie today and get verbal commitment.
2) Contracts (cc'd in thread) — prepare a redlined addendum and a renewal term sheet reflecting the $40k credit and 12-month commitment. Use redlined_addendum.pdf as working doc (attached).
3) Grace — prepare incident summary and mitigations plan to include with the renewal package.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
